acceptance_cases.counterexample: An inner occurrence claim stores the final OwnedSettlementV2 root and makes its own canonical preimage recursive.
acceptance_cases.given: The exact local occurrence claim is nested inside OwnedSettlementV2.
acceptance_cases.invariant: No value inside the settlement depends on owned_settlement_root_v2.
nonclaims: Acyclicity does not authenticate the settlement.
This case does not authorize a codec implementation.
acceptance_cases.then: The self-root field and every backward dependency edge reject.
acceptance_cases.title: Settlement root dependency is acyclic
acceptance_cases.when: The dependency graph and inner-claim field registry are checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: An occurrence ID derived from command_root is stored inside the settlement that command_root hashes.
acceptance_cases.given: The command root commits the exact admitted settlement and intent tuple.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Command-derived occurrence IDs exist only in controlled evidence after command_root is known.
nonclaims: The command schema and domain separator remain to be frozen.
An occurrence ID does not prove current-state provenance.
acceptance_cases.then: The inner occurrence_id field and any command-root cycle reject.
acceptance_cases.title: Occurrence identity is derived after command identity
acceptance_cases.when: The inner-claim registry and dependency graph are checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: The settlement root projection omits provisional claims, allowing unequal settlements to share one root.
acceptance_cases.given: OwnedSettlementV2 contains one mandatory exact occurrence-claim tuple.
acceptance_cases.invariant: The full canonical settlement envelope includes the complete occurrence-claim tuple.
nonclaims: Hash commitment does not establish semantic correctness.
SHA-256 collision resistance is assumed.
acceptance_cases.then: Any omission or blanking projection is rejected by the exact root strategy.
acceptance_cases.title: Settlement root commits every local occurrence claim
acceptance_cases.when: The root strategy and outer field registry are checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A caller supplies a matching settlement root and claim tuple without fresh replay from the exact pre-state.
acceptance_cases.given: The exact current state, authenticated command, validated configuration, and authenticated context remain present.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Expected, admitted, and consumed claim tuples are exactly equal before controlled evidence exists.
nonclaims: The current replay kernel is unmounted.
This relation does not prove datastore currentness.
acceptance_cases.then: Coordinated claim and root substitution rejects against fresh source-bound replay.
acceptance_cases.title: Claim tuple equality is source-bound
acceptance_cases.when: The controlled derivation sources and equality gate are checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A shell selects configuration, pre-state, command, or context roots independently of their authenticated sources.
acceptance_cases.given: Every authority-bearing root has one independently retained source value.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Submitted roots are equality targets and never independent authority inputs.
nonclaims: The exact authentication mechanisms remain later checkpoints.
A validated configuration claim carries no state authority by itself.
acceptance_cases.then: The controlled batch is derived only after point-of-use reconstruction of every root.
acceptance_cases.title: Independent sources remain present through binding
acceptance_cases.when: The source-role registry and graph predecessors are checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A zero-valued fee claim creates duplicate or economically empty lineage.
acceptance_cases.given: The mandatory occurrence-claim tuple may be empty.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Only a strictly positive provisional protocol fee produces an inner occurrence claim.
nonclaims: A zero-fee fill may still appear in the settlement fill tuple.
This does not change quote or fill semantics.
acceptance_cases.then: Zero provisional fee produces no claim and positive fee produces exactly one fill-bound claim.
acceptance_cases.title: Zero fee has one canonical absence representation
acceptance_cases.when: The claim cardinality policy is checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: An earlier failure leaves a replay candidate, witness batch, receipt, bundle, or effect plan.
acceptance_cases.given: Decode, admission, validation, replay, equality, and binding are ordered phases.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Every rejection before controlled derivation carries no authority-bearing output.
nonclaims: Committed-failure semantics are outside this checkpoint.
No publication shell is implemented.
acceptance_cases.then: The no-successor output list remains complete and closed.
acceptance_cases.title: Early rejection is authority-empty
acceptance_cases.when: The rejection authority registry is checked.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A design-only carrier clarification is treated as permission to mount V2 settlement authority.
acceptance_cases.given: The exact carrier and controlled-batch schemas still require independent review.
acceptance_cases.invariant: This contract remains design-only and unmounted.
nonclaims: No V2 settlement carrier is implemented by this contract.
No runtime, receipt, bundle, proof, or datastore path is approved.
acceptance_cases.then: Implementation and mount authority remain false.
acceptance_cases.title: Design evidence cannot promote runtime authority
acceptance_cases.when: The phase flags and nonclaim set are checked.

nonclaims: OwnedSettlementV2 admission and canonical codecs are not implemented.
The controlled witness batch is not implemented.
The command schema and root preimage are not frozen.
No state, configuration, receipt, bundle, proof, publication, or mount authority exists.
Python and Rust parity is not established.

source_roles.validated_active_configuration_v2: point-of-use B1A-validated active configuration bound to exact state
